run.question: Our analytics dashboard seems slow. Can you check the shard configuration for the app-186-shard-analytics index? How many primary shards does it have and what is their status?

report.summary: I checked the index app-186-shard-analytics directly: it exists, is open and green, and has 7 primary shards with 0 replicas (9bf1095a-aa29-4bff-af26-ed663b488320-t0:6dc761b3-5040-49c0-8084-92b3f8f3d9c8, 9bf1095a-aa29-4bff-af26-ed663b488320-t1:e50483f8-cb4e-4d9b-ae89-f6b0cd2aea47). Shard-level data confirms all 7 primaries (shard 0 through 6) are in state STARTED on the single node bea971fdc0c6 (172.17.0.2); six of them hold 0 docs at 227b each and shard 5 holds the index's single document at 4.6kb (179ee779-f922-4ad8-a0f0-848538b51ade-t0:9bf51713-e64f-48b6-8127-10c0a1ddd5ae). The index-level shard health view reports number_of_shards 7, active_primary_shards 7, active_shards 7 and 0 unassigned, initializing or relocating shards, so the shard configuration is fully allocated and healthy as observed (179ee779-f922-4ad8-a0f0-848538b51ade-t1:d9b81bee-3ed9-43ac-8a78-599e55707f0a). Nothing in this shard configuration or status indicates a fault: there are no unassigned, initializing or relocating primaries and no replica shards to be unavailable. Therefore this index's shard layout does not explain the slow analytics dashboard on the evidence gathered; the cause of the reported slowness remains unidentified. As context only, the cluster reports a single node (number_of_nodes 1, number_of_data_nodes 1) with 510 active primary shards and green status, and this index's cumulative search counters read query_total 0 and query_time_in_millis 0 (8aafaefb-3aaf-4dc8-80de-400083793669-t1:e9efc470-5e26-4c22-8943-bcb1e661cf98, 8aafaefb-3aaf-4dc8-80de-400083793669-t0:9703bb5a-149f-4908-9e5f-6bfe84f49117). Because those counters are cumulative since the index/node started and are not windowed, and because all six delivered views report state at query time only, no statement is made about search latency or shard state during the incident window.

claims.text: Index app-186-shard-analytics exists with health green, status open, pri=7 (7 primary shards) and rep=0 (no replicas), docs.count 1 and store.size 5.9kb.

_cat/shards for app-186-shard-analytics returns exactly 7 rows, all prirep=p, shards 0,1,2,3,4,5,6, every one in state STARTED on node bea971fdc0c6 (ip 172.17.0.2); shard 5 carries the 1 document (store 4.6kb) and the other six carry 0 documents (store 227b each).

Index-level cluster health for app-186-shard-analytics reports status green, number_of_shards 7, number_of_replicas 0, active_primary_shards 7, active_shards 7, and 0 unassigned, initializing or relocating shards, with primary_active true for each of shards 0 through 6.
Cluster-wide health returns status green, number_of_nodes 1, number_of_data_nodes 1, active_primary_shards 510, active_shards 510, and 0 unassigned, initializing or relocating shards.

Index stats for app-186-shard-analytics show cumulative counters query_total 0, query_time_in_millis 0, fetch_total 0 and fetch_time_in_millis 0 on the primaries, with docs.count 1 and store size_in_bytes 6143; these are cumulative since the index/node started, not counts inside the incident window.

All 7 primary shards of app-186-shard-analytics are allocated to the same single node bea971fdc0c6, and the cluster reports only one data node, so the index has no replica copy and no second node to serve reads; this is an observed topology fact, not evidence of failure.

The reported analytics-dashboard slowness is not caused by app-186-shard-analytics shard configuration or shard status, since all 7 primaries are STARTED and allocated with no unassigned, initializing or relocating shards, and the index holds a single 5.9kb document; a cause outside this index or outside shard health generally would have to be shown by other evidence.

If dashboard latency must be explained, capture time-bounded search latency (index search query_time_in_millis and fetch_time_in_millis deltas, or slow-query logs) for app-186-shard-analytics and the other indices the dashboard reads, since the cluster holds 510 primary shards on a single data node and no windowed latency series was available in this Run.

gaps: No time-bounded shard, allocation or health history was available: all six delivered Elasticsearch views state they reflect state at the moment of the query, so shard status during the incident window (2026-10-24T17:36:26Z to 2026-11-23T17:36:26Z) is unknown.

No windowed search-latency signal was obtained for app-186-shard-analytics; the only search metrics available (query_total 0, query_time_in_millis 0, fetch_total 0) are cumulative counters and cannot be attributed to the incident window, so the dashboard slowness is unexplained.
Whether the analytics dashboard queries app-186-shard-analytics at all could not be verified.
The cluster reports 510 active primary shards across indices; only app-186-shard-analytics was examined, so shard pressure on other indices the dashboard may read is unchecked.
No application-tier or dashboard-tier performance telemetry or logs were queried, so the user-perceived latency has no observed source in this Run.
The change_history integration is not integrated in this Run, so any configuration or scale change that might explain the slowness could not be reviewed.
next_steps: Collect time-series search latency and slow-query evidence for the indices the analytics dashboard actually queries, over the incident window rather than an instantaneous reading.
Review search thread-pool queue and rejected metrics plus node stats to see whether 510 primary shards on one data node are contending for search capacity.
Confirm with the dashboard owners which index pattern the slow panels use, and whether app-186-shard-analytics participates at all.
Assess whether 7 shards for a 1-document, 5.9kb analytics index matches the intended sizing; this is a sizing-advisory question, not an observed fault.
